stage1.text: 2. Standalone unit economics & break-even cushion (Priority 2 — downside resilience)

children.text: Hypothesis: At $8/order CM and $800/day fixed cost ($560 labor + $240 lease), standalone break-even is 100/day and network break-even is 125/day

exemplars.stage3:
Proceed with Location 2 only if the landlord grants a $24,000 tenant-improvement (TI) allowance or reduces rent to $6,000/month to bring cannibalization-adjusted payback under 14 months.

Diagnosis: On a standalone basis, Westside looks attractive: each order generates $8.00 contribution margin ($12.00 AOV - $4.00 variable cost), or $1,200/day at 150 customers. Against $800/day in fixed costs ($560 labor + $240/day for the $7,200 monthly lease), Westside breaks even at 100 customers/day, earns $400/day ($12,000/month), and pays back the $108,000 buildout in 9.0 months. However, because 25 of those daily customers are cannibalized from Downtown (costing 25 x $8 x 30 = $6,000/month in lost Location 1 profit), net incremental profit across both shops is only $6,000/month ($200/day). That raises the effective network break-even to 125 customers/day and doubles true payback to 18.0 months.

Recommendations:
1. Counter-offer the lease: request a $24,000 TI credit (cutting net buildout to $84,000, or 14-month net payback) or match Downtown's $6,000/month rent (+$1,200/month cash flow, cutting net payback to 15 months).
2. Protect Downtown traffic: launch a Downtown-only afternoon pickup bundle so existing regulars do not defect.

Risks & Mitigation: With a network break-even of 125 customers/day, a 17% shortfall in Westside traffic (falling from 150 to 125/day) wipes out all incremental profit. Mitigate by staging staffing at $480/day during the first 60 days.

Next Step: Before signing, run a 2-week zip-code check on Downtown POS receipts and a weekend Westside pop-up; sign only if projected net new Westside demand exceeds 130 non-Downtown customers/day.
